scenarios.task: Set `max_retries` in `config/webhooks/payment_events.yaml`: how many times the payment-events webhook consumer retries a failed delivery. Give the number.

current.memo: Payment-events webhook consumer: max_retries is 6. The provider redelivers for six attempts on its side, and matching that count avoids duplicate-charge reconciliation alerts.

stale.memo: Payment-events webhook consumer: max_retries is 3, the client library default. Failing fast means the on-call page fires early when the provider is down.

adjacent.memo: Email-notification webhook consumer: max_retries is 12, because the mail relay throttles in bursts. This applies only to the notifications consumer; the payment consumers belong to the payments team and set their own limits.

contra_a.memo: Payment-events webhook consumer retries 4 times. More than that overlaps with the nightly settlement batch and double-books the ledger lock.

contra_b.memo: Payment-events webhook consumer retries 9 times, so that an hour-long provider outage is absorbed without a manual replay.

scenarios.task: Set `TIMESTAMP_ZONE` in `audit/format.py`: the time zone every audit-log timestamp is written in. Give the IANA zone name.

current.memo: Audit log timestamps are written in Europe/Dublin. The Irish entity's regulator requires local wall-clock time in every audit extract.

stale.memo: Audit log timestamps are written in UTC so that entries from every region sort together without conversion.

adjacent.memo: The US billing export writes its timestamps in America/New_York, as the US bank's file specification requires. That rule is part of the bank file format only and says nothing about the application's own logs, including the audit log.

contra_a.memo: Audit log timestamps use Europe/London, because the compliance team that reads them sits in London.

contra_b.memo: Audit log timestamps use Europe/Amsterdam to match the data centre the audit store is hosted in.

scenarios.task: Set `DELIMITER` for the monthly ledger CSV export in `exports/ledger.py`. Give the name of the delimiter character as a word.

current.memo: Monthly ledger CSV export uses a semicolon delimiter. The accounting team opens it in spreadsheet software set to a European locale, where commas are decimal separators.

stale.memo: Monthly ledger CSV export uses a comma delimiter, the plain RFC 4180 default.

adjacent.memo: The warehouse bulk-load files use a tab delimiter, because the loader's CSV mode chokes on quoted newlines. This is the loader's input format only; files meant for people, such as the ledger exports, are not covered by it.

contra_a.memo: Monthly ledger CSV export uses a pipe delimiter, since vendor names routinely contain commas and semicolons.

contra_b.memo: Monthly ledger CSV export uses a colon delimiter, which the finance team's import macros are written for.

scenarios.task: Set `python-version` for the test job in `.github/workflows/test.yml`. Give the version number.

current.memo: The CI test job runs on Python 3.12, the version the production workers run.

stale.memo: The CI test job runs on Python 3.10, matching the production worker image.

adjacent.memo: The Airflow DAG repository is pinned to Python 3.9 by the managed scheduler service. That pin belongs to the DAG repository only; this repository's own CI follows the worker image.

contra_a.memo: The CI test job runs on Python 3.11, the version the data team's notebooks use.

contra_b.memo: The CI test job runs on Python 3.13, so that deprecation warnings show up a release ahead of production.

scenarios.task: Set `DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE` for the public `/v2/products` endpoint in `api/pagination.py`. Give the number.

current.memo: Public /v2/products default page size is 40. The storefront grid shows 40 tiles per page, so one request fills one page view.

stale.memo: Public /v2/products default page size is 25, the value from the original API style guide.

adjacent.memo: The internal admin export API pages at 200 rows, because it is only called by batch jobs. It is a separate service from the public API, and none of its limits apply to public endpoints.

contra_a.memo: Public /v2/products default page size is 50; the mobile app requests exactly one page per screen at that size.

contra_b.memo: Public /v2/products default page size is 30, the size the storefront design specifies for the web grid.

scenarios.task: Set `PRICE_TTL_SECONDS` in `cache/prices.py`: how long product-price lookups are cached. Give the number of seconds.

current.memo: Product-price lookups are cached for 90 seconds. Flash sales change prices at short notice, and a longer cache would charge customers a price that has already ended.

stale.memo: Product-price lookups are cached for 3600 seconds, since prices only change in the nightly catalogue sync.

adjacent.memo: Product image URLs are cached for 86400 seconds at the CDN, because images are content-addressed and never change in place. This is an image caching rule only; prices and stock are cached by their own services.

contra_a.memo: Product-price lookups are cached for 300 seconds, the most the pricing database can take without read replicas.

contra_b.memo: Product-price lookups are cached for 15 seconds, because the finance team requires prices to be near real time.

scenarios.task: Set `ARTIFACT_BUCKET` in `deploy/staging.env`: the object-storage bucket staging training jobs write model artifacts to. Give the bucket name.

current.memo: Staging training jobs write model artifacts to lumen-stg-artifacts-eu2, in the same region as the GPU pool, which avoids cross-region egress.

stale.memo: Staging training jobs write model artifacts to lumen-staging-artifacts.

adjacent.memo: Staging training datasets are read from lumen-ingest-raw, which is read-only for jobs by policy. It holds input datasets only; where jobs write their outputs is decided separately.

contra_a.memo: Staging training jobs write model artifacts to lumen-stg-models, the bucket the model registry watches.

contra_b.memo: Staging training jobs write model artifacts to lumen-ml-stage-out, which has the short lifecycle policy that keeps staging storage costs down.

scenarios.task: Set `LOG_LEVEL` for the production gateway in `deploy/prod/gateway.env`. Give the level name.

current.memo: Production gateway runs at LOG_LEVEL WARNING. Per-request log lines would cost more in log ingestion than the gateway's compute.

stale.memo: Production gateway runs at LOG_LEVEL INFO so that every request line is searchable during incidents.

adjacent.memo: The auth sidecar runs at DEBUG in production until the token-refresh investigation closes. The sidecar is its own deployment with its own env file; the gateway's settings are unaffected.

contra_a.memo: Production gateway runs at LOG_LEVEL ERROR; request tracing covers everything below that.

contra_b.memo: Production gateway runs at LOG_LEVEL NOTICE, the level the log shipper's alert rules are keyed on.

scenarios.task: Set the base image in the `FROM` line of `worker/Dockerfile`. Give the image reference.

current.memo: Worker Dockerfile builds FROM python:3.12-slim-bookworm. Pinning the Debian release keeps glibc stable for the PDF renderer.

stale.memo: Worker Dockerfile builds FROM python:3.10-slim.

adjacent.memo: The frontend build stage uses node:20-alpine. That image is for the static asset build only; the Python worker image is chosen by the backend team.

contra_a.memo: Worker Dockerfile builds FROM python:3.12-alpine, to keep the image small for the autoscaler's cold starts.

contra_b.memo: Worker Dockerfile builds FROM debian:bookworm-slim and installs Python from the distribution, so that security patches arrive with the OS updates.

scenarios.task: Set `MAX_UPLOAD_MB` for document uploads in `settings/uploads.py`. Give the number of megabytes.

current.memo: Document uploads are capped at 35 MB. Scanned contracts from the enterprise tier run large, and 35 MB covers every one seen in the last quarter.

stale.memo: Document uploads are capped at 10 MB to keep the virus scanner under its time budget.

adjacent.memo: The video ingestion service accepts uploads up to 500 MB through its resumable endpoint. That service and its limits are separate from the document upload path.

contra_a.memo: Document uploads are capped at 20 MB, the figure in the storage cost model agreed with finance.

contra_b.memo: Document uploads are capped at 64 MB, the figure in the storage cost model agreed with finance.

scenarios.task: Set `ROUNDING_MODE` for invoice line totals in `billing/money.py`. Give the constant name from Python's decimal module.

current.memo: Invoice line totals round with ROUND_HALF_EVEN, which keeps monthly totals in line with the payment processor's settlement files.

stale.memo: Invoice line totals round with ROUND_HALF_UP, the way customers expect from school arithmetic.

adjacent.memo: The VAT return report truncates with ROUND_DOWN, as the tax authority's filing guide prescribes. That rule covers the tax report only and does not apply to customer invoices.

contra_a.memo: Invoice line totals round with ROUND_UP, so that the company never under-bills on fractional usage.

contra_b.memo: Invoice line totals round with ROUND_FLOOR, so that customers are never over-billed on fractional usage.

scenarios.task: Set `METRICS_PORT` for the scheduler service in `scheduler/config.toml`. Give the port number.

current.memo: Scheduler exposes metrics on port 9464, the OpenTelemetry Prometheus exporter port the collector scrapes by default.

stale.memo: Scheduler exposes metrics on port 9090.

adjacent.memo: Host-level metrics come from the node exporter on port 9100 on every machine. That port belongs to the host agent; services pick their own metrics ports.

contra_a.memo: Scheduler exposes metrics on port 8081, next to its admin API on 8080.

contra_b.memo: Scheduler exposes metrics on port 9300, the port reserved for scheduler metrics in the team's port registry.

scenarios.task: Set `DEFAULT_LOCALE` for the editor UI in `editor/i18n.ts`. Give the locale code.

current.memo: Editor UI default locale is en-GB. Most editors are in the UK and house style uses British spellings.

stale.memo: Editor UI default locale is en-US, the framework default.

adjacent.memo: The white-label portal for the Berlin partner defaults to de-DE. That setting lives in the partner's portal build and does not affect the core editor.

contra_a.memo: Editor UI default locale is en-IE, since most of the editorial team is based in Dublin.

contra_b.memo: Editor UI default locale is fr-FR, since most of the editorial team is based in Montreal.

scenarios.task: Set `THUMBNAIL_QUEUE` in `jobs/queues.py`: the queue thumbnail-generation tasks are published to. Give the queue name.

current.memo: Thumbnail-generation tasks publish to media.thumbs.v2, the queue whose payload carries the crop hints the thumbnail workers expect.

stale.memo: Thumbnail-generation tasks publish to the thumbnails queue.

adjacent.memo: Video transcoding tasks publish to video-transcode-jobs. Only transcoding jobs go there; image work has its own queues.

contra_a.memo: Thumbnail-generation tasks publish to media.thumbs, the queue the thumbnail workers subscribe to.

contra_b.memo: Thumbnail-generation tasks publish to img-thumbnails-high, the priority queue, because thumbnail rendering blocks the upload confirmation screen.

scenarios.task: Set `line-length` under `[tool.ruff]` in `pyproject.toml`. Give the number.

current.memo: Ruff line-length is 100. The long type annotations in the plugin API wrap into unreadable shapes at narrower widths.

stale.memo: Ruff line-length is 88, the Black default, so formatting matches the upstream projects we contribute to.

adjacent.memo: The generated client SDK repository uses line-length 120, because the generator emits long lines that cannot be wrapped. That setting is for generated code only; hand-written repositories keep their own style.

contra_a.memo: Ruff line-length is 79, so that side-by-side diffs fit on a laptop screen.

contra_b.memo: Ruff line-length is 110, so that the plugin API's long signatures fit on one line.

scenarios.task: Set `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_MS` for calls from the search API to the ranking service in `search/clients.py`. Give the number of milliseconds.

current.memo: Search API calls to the ranking service time out after 850 ms. Past that the fallback lexical ranking returns faster than waiting, and the p99 latency budget is 1 second.

stale.memo: Search API calls to the ranking service time out after 2000 ms.

adjacent.memo: The batch reindexer calls the ranking service with a 15000 ms timeout, since it scores large batches offline. That timeout is for the reindexer only; interactive callers set their own.

contra_a.memo: Search API calls to the ranking service time out after 500 ms, per the ranking team's service-level objective.

contra_b.memo: Search API calls to the ranking service time out after 1200 ms, to ride out the ranking service's garbage-collection pauses.

scenarios.task: Name the environment variable `auth/settings.py` reads the JWT signing key from. Give the variable name.

current.memo: The auth service reads its JWT signing key from WREN_JWT_SIGNING_KEY. The prefix keeps the key from colliding with other tools' variables in the shared secrets injector.

stale.memo: The auth service reads its JWT signing key from JWT_SECRET.

adjacent.memo: Outgoing partner webhooks are signed with the key in PARTNER_HOOK_SECRET. That key is for webhook signatures only and must never be used for user tokens.

contra_a.memo: The auth service reads its JWT signing key from AUTH_SIGNING_KEY, the name the platform's secret template generates.

contra_b.memo: The auth service reads its JWT signing key from WREN_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY, since tokens are signed with an asymmetric key pair.

scenarios.task: Set `DB_POOL_SIZE` for the orders API workers in `orders/db.py`. Give the number.

current.memo: Orders API workers use DB_POOL_SIZE 14. At the present worker count, 14 per worker keeps the total under the database's connection limit with room for migrations.

stale.memo: Orders API workers use DB_POOL_SIZE 5, the driver default.

adjacent.memo: The analytics consumer uses a pool of 40 against the read replica. It is a separate process on a separate database, and its pool says nothing about the orders API.

contra_a.memo: Orders API workers use DB_POOL_SIZE 8; load tests showed no gain beyond that.

contra_b.memo: Orders API workers use DB_POOL_SIZE 20, to absorb the checkout spikes at the top of the hour.

scenarios.task: Set `COMPRESSION` for the nightly archive tarballs in `archive/pack.py`. Give the codec name.

current.memo: Nightly archive tarballs use zstd. It compresses well at little CPU cost, which keeps the archive job inside its window.

stale.memo: Nightly archive tarballs use gzip, since every restore host can read it.

adjacent.memo: The live replication stream is compressed with lz4 for latency. That choice is for the streaming path only; batch archives are a separate decision.

contra_a.memo: Nightly archive tarballs use xz, for the best ratio on cold storage priced per gigabyte.

contra_b.memo: Nightly archive tarballs use bzip2, which the restore scripts expect.

scenarios.task: Set `PRIMARY_REGION` for the customer-data database in `infra/db.tf`. Give the region identifier.

current.memo: The customer-data database's primary region is eu-central-2, the Zurich region, since the Swiss customers' contracts require data residency in Switzerland.

stale.memo: The customer-data database's primary region is us-east-1, next to the rest of the stack.

adjacent.memo: The marketing site's CDN origin is in eu-west-1. It holds no customer data and has no bearing on where customer databases live.

contra_a.memo: The customer-data database's primary region is eu-central-1, which satisfies EU residency and has every managed service we use.

contra_b.memo: The customer-data database's primary region is eu-north-1, chosen for its lower storage prices.

scenarios.task: Set `RETENTION_DAYS` for application logs in `logging/retention.yaml`. Give the number of days.

current.memo: Application logs are retained for 45 days. The logs contain IP addresses, so the privacy policy caps retention, and 45 days still covers the monthly billing dispute window.

stale.memo: Application logs are retained for 90 days.

adjacent.memo: Security audit logs are retained for 400 days under the legal hold policy. That hold covers the security audit trail only, not application logs.

contra_a.memo: Application logs are retained for 30 days, the storage tier's included allowance.

contra_b.memo: Application logs are retained for 60 days, so that two full incident-review cycles can reference them.

scenarios.task: Set `PASSWORD_HASHER` in `accounts/security.py`. Give the algorithm name.

current.memo: User passwords are hashed with argon2id. The security policy requires a memory-hard function.

stale.memo: User passwords are hashed with bcrypt.

adjacent.memo: API keys are stored hashed with scrypt by the key service. That service handles machine credentials only; user password hashing is owned by the accounts module.

contra_a.memo: User passwords are hashed with pbkdf2_sha256, the algorithm the identity team standardised on for every service.

contra_b.memo: User passwords are hashed with argon2i, the algorithm the platform security team standardised on for every service.

scenarios.task: Set `DEPLOY_BRANCH` in `.deploy/config.yml`: the git branch whose pushes deploy to production. Give the branch name.

current.memo: Production deploys from pushes to the release-train branch. Merges to release-train require a second approval, which keeps half-reviewed changes out of production.

stale.memo: Production deploys from pushes to main.

adjacent.memo: The documentation site publishes from the gh-pages branch. That applies to the docs site only; the application's deploy pipeline is configured separately.

contra_a.memo: Production deploys from pushes to prod-stable, which only the release manager can push to.

contra_b.memo: Production deploys from pushes to deploy/production, tagged weekly from the integration branch.

scenarios.task: Set `EXPORT_ENCODING` for the contacts CSV export in `crm/export.py`. Give the Python codec name.

current.memo: Contacts CSV export is written as utf-8-sig. The sales team's spreadsheet software needs the byte-order mark to read accented surnames correctly.

stale.memo: Contacts CSV export is written as utf-8.

adjacent.memo: Files for the legacy accounting import are written in cp1252, the only encoding that system reads. That constraint belongs to the accounting integration and not to user-facing exports.

contra_a.memo: Contacts CSV export is written as utf-16, which the CRM's import wizard detects automatically.

contra_b.memo: Contacts CSV export is written as iso-8859-15, the encoding the sales team's mail-merge templates are saved in.

distractors.memo: Stand-up moved to the afternoon slot on Tuesdays so the design team can attend.
Run `make lint` before pushing; CI runs the same target, so a clean local run means a clean CI lint step.
The design system's typeface is Inter. Do not add other font families to the web bundle.
On-call handoff happens on Monday mornings, in the incident channel, with a written summary of open alerts.
Pull request titles follow Conventional Commits, since the changelog generator parses them.
The staging database is reset from anonymised production data every Sunday night. Do not keep test fixtures there.
The session-expiry test is quarantined as flaky while the clock-mocking library is replaced. Do not delete it.
Dashboards live in the observability repository as code. Edits made in the dashboard UI are overwritten on the next sync.
Screenshots in the docs are captured at double resolution and saved as PNG.
Dependency update pull requests are batched weekly, and are merged on Wednesdays after the integration suite passes.
Do not use print for diagnostics; use the structured logger, which attaches the request identifier automatically.
The mobile app ships every second Thursday. Features that miss a date wait for the next one.
Legal must review any new cookie or local-storage key before it ships.
Pair with a second engineer on any migration that rewrites a large table, and run it outside business hours.
The integration tests need Docker running locally; they start their own containers and remove them afterwards.
The changelog is generated from pull request labels. Do not edit the changelog file by hand.
The badges at the top of the README are generated by a script in the tools folder.
No production deploys during the team offsite week; the freeze is announced in the engineering channel.
Reviewers should leave a summary comment stating whether their remarks are blocking.
Every new form field needs a visible label; placeholder text alone failed the accessibility audit.
